direct_file_reviews.summary: Prompt defines the Python deepdiff script, Node ESM .mjs output requirement, manual argv parsing, byte-for-byte output alignment, zero external dependencies, and black-box executable probing.
Parallel metadata reports actual_parallel_used true, four subagents, finished process, completed evaluation, artifact copied, and official aggregate quality of 67/70 with solution_passed false.
Current completed status evaluation is the authoritative outcome: RepoZero Py2JS evaluator completed, task_result is 67 passed of 70, and solution_passed is false.
Evaluation summary repeats the completed official Docker evaluator result with 67/70 samples passed and solution_passed false.

timeline_reviews.summary: Server event stream is transport-only in the manifest and contributes no semantic task actions to the projected ledger.
Session index maps the parallel session id to the workspace directory and is transport-only with no implementation actions.
Child agent-0 owned pyrepr.mjs, wrote Python-style repr and print helpers, ran 19 focused checks, and returned a completed slice.
Child agent-1 first wrote deepdiff.mjs, then after parent follow-up added pydifflib.mjs and multiline string diff support, fixed a syntax issue, and verified both unit and differential cases.
Child agent-2 owned extract.mjs and argparse.mjs, wrote both utilities, checked normal extraction, parser success, error, and help behavior, then cleaned temporary files.
Child agent-3 owned only test11.mjs, wrote the entry file against the pinned interfaces, saw dependencies were not all present yet, and performed a syntax check only.

The parent probed reference behavior, launched AgentSwarm with pinned module interfaces, received all child results, ran integrated differential checks, discovered a multiline DeepDiff gap, resumed agent-1 with exact findings, and reverified 18 cases plus ESM import constraints.

direct_file_reviews.summary: Prompt is byte-matched to the parallel prompt and defines the same Python-to-Node ESM migration requirements and executable probing allowance.
Serial metadata reports no parallel uptake, no subagents, finished process, completed evaluation, artifact copied, and official aggregate quality of 67/70 with solution_passed false.
Current completed status evaluation is the authoritative outcome for serial: official evaluator completed, task_result is 67 passed of 70, and solution_passed is false.
Evaluation summary repeats the completed official Docker evaluator result with 67/70 samples passed and solution_passed false.

timeline_reviews.summary: Server event stream is transport-only in the manifest and contributes no semantic task actions to the projected ledger.
Session index maps the serial session id to the workspace directory and is transport-only with no implementation actions.
The single serial actor probed reference output and argument errors, wrote pyrepr.mjs, deepdiff.mjs, argparse.mjs, and test11.mjs itself, then verified normal and error paths before finalizing.

parallel.requirements: The parent recognized the ESM .mjs, zero external dependency, manual argv parsing, byte-for-byte output, black-box probing, module split, and /output delivery requirements. It also later discovered a multiline DeepDiff diff-key behavior through executable probing.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent decomposed work into four distinct child slices: pyrepr, deepdiff, extract plus argparse, and test11 entry. The parent retained integration and verification ownership and later resumed the deepdiff child for a focused fix.
parallel.implementation: Children wrote separate modules with pinned exports. Agent-1 first implemented core diff behavior, then after the parent discovered multiline string diff output, added pydifflib.mjs and updated deepdiff.mjs to include the diff key.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Children wrote directly into /output using separate file ownership. The final artifact list contains pyrepr.mjs, pydifflib.mjs, deepdiff.mjs, extract.mjs, argparse.mjs, and test11.mjs.
parallel.verification: The parent ran integrated differential checks, found one multiline mismatch, probed the reference executable further, delegated the fix, then independently ran 18 differential cases and a dependency-rule grep fallback.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Despite local verification success, the current official evaluator marked the solution failed with 67/70. The mounted summaries do not identify the three failing samples, so no specific final code defect can be proven from evaluator detail.

serial.requirements: The serial actor recognized the same ESM, zero dependency, manual argv parsing, output parity, executable probing, and /output delivery requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: The single actor kept all ownership locally, designing and writing pyrepr.mjs, deepdiff.mjs, argparse.mjs, and test11.mjs without delegation or child handoffs.
serial.implementation: The serial implementation wrote a compact DeepDiff and extract in deepdiff.mjs, a parser in argparse.mjs, Python-style repr helpers, and the entry file. It did not show the later pydifflib multiline unified-diff support present in parallel.
serial.integration_and_delivery: All modules were written by the same actor and verified in /output; the artifact list contains test11.mjs, argparse.mjs, pyrepr.mjs, and deepdiff.mjs.
serial.verification: Serial compared normal stdout cases, leading-zero and signed integers, quote handling, and normalized program-name differences for error paths. It did not show multiline DeepDiff differential tests.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The current official evaluator also marked serial failed with 67/70. The observed process leaves multiline string diff support unimplemented, but the mounted evaluator data does not identify which three samples failed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the written migration requirements and, during verification, discovered an additional observable DeepDiff multiline-string output behavior.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same written prompt requirements and probed standard output and argument behavior but did not surface multiline DeepDiff behavior.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The explicit task requirements were the same; the parallel run learned and implemented one additional black-box behavior, while serial stopped at the simpler observed cases.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel delegated four file groups to child agents with distinct file ownership and kept parent-level verification responsibility.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all implementation, integration, and verification work in one actor.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced handoffs and separate module ownership; serial avoided coordination boundaries by using a single implementation owner.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel parent pinned exact export names and cross-file contracts in the AgentSwarm prompt and later sent a detailed follow-up brief to agent-1.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used internal interfaces it designed itself, importing its own ArgumentParser, deepDiff, extract, and pyStr functions.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel needed explicit cross-agent contracts, which were present and used; serial had no cross-agent interface boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ended with separate pyrepr, pydifflib, deepdiff, extract, argparse, and entry modules, including a pydifflib port for multiline string diffs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ended with pyrepr, deepdiff, argparse, and entry modules, with extract bundled in deepdiff and no pydifflib module or multiline diff-key implementation evident.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel implemented a broader DeepDiff behavior surface after finding a mismatch; serial used a simpler black-box reimplementation that covered the cases it tested.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent received the initial AgentSwarm result, inspected integrated behavior, then resumed agent-1 and received the follow-up result before final checks.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; the actor wrote and tested files directly.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had child returns and a follow-up result to manage, but the needed returned work was consumed before closure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children wrote different files in the same /output workspace; the parent then listed and tested the assembled file set.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote all files itself in /output and then ran differential tests against the assembled local output.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had shared-workspace writes but with distinct file ownership and no observed overwrite, collision, or provenance instability; serial had no shared writer.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel performed reference probing, initial integrated differential checks, multiline-specific probes, child-level unit and differential tests, final 18-case differential checks, and dependency-rule grep fallback.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial verified five normal cases and normalized error-path behavior, then declared all checks passed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had broader observed verification, especially for multiline values; both still failed official evaluation with the same aggregate score.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used four subagents, 42 LLM requests, and about 1028 agent seconds, finishing without timeout and with official evaluation completed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no subagents, 8 LLM requests, and about 278 agent seconds, also finishing without timeout and with official evaluation completed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent much more budget on swarm coordination and broader verification, but no timeout or deadline displacement is evidenced; both closed normally and failed officially.

outcome_analysis.explanation: There is no discordant official outcome in the current completed status records: parallel and serial both failed official evaluation with 67/70. The concrete task-solving difference is that parallel used child modules and later fixed a discovered multiline DeepDiff diff-key gap through a resumed child, while serial implemented locally and did not show that multiline behavior. Because both official outcomes and aggregate scores are identical, this difference is a strategy and implementation-path contrast rather than a proven outcome cause.
parallel_contributors: Four-agent decomposition produced separate modules and parent-owned integration.
Parent differential testing discovered multiline DeepDiff behavior and sent a detailed follow-up to agent-1.
The parent reverified 18 differential cases and dependency constraints before closure.
serial_contributors: Single actor wrote all modules directly without handoffs.
Verification covered normal and argument-error behavior but not the multiline diff behavior seen in parallel.
The final serial summary did not include pydifflib or multiline unified-diff support.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel added pydifflib.mjs and multiline string diff entries; serial did not.
Serial bundled extract into deepdiff.mjs and used its own ArgumentParser abstraction, while parallel split extract and argparse into separate child-owned modules.
The mounted official summaries do not expose the specific three failed samples, so the remaining final defects cannot be assigned to a specific ordinary code path.
evaluator_effects: Only aggregate official pass counts are mounted; no sample-level failure identities are available in the allowed inputs.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no official outcome difference; supported comparative strategy and implementation contrast only

candidates.reason: Implementation ownership was assigned to child slices and the parent; files were actually written, so implementation was not ownerless.
The parent explicitly retained integration and verification responsibility and performed integrated differential checks after child completion.
The entry file was assigned to agent-3 and final artifact validation found the expected test11.mjs entry present.
The parent carried the end-to-end transition from probing through child delegation, result inspection, integrated testing, follow-up, and final response.
The parent ran brief executable probes before delegation, but productive child implementation was not blocked behind a long mandatory preflight causing unfinished work.
There was not a separate all-investigation phase that left implementation deadline constrained; implementation proceeded via the swarm after limited probing and completed.
No indispensable path was starved: the parent resumed the deepdiff path when it became critical and completed final verification before closure.
Although the run used four subagents and more tokens than serial, it did not time out and there is no evidence that fan-out consumed the budget before required work or verification.
No child was left with an overbroad unfinished assignment; agent-1's larger follow-up completed, and the parent consumed it.
The child briefs included known task, file, interface, and verification requirements. The later multiline diff fact was discovered after initial delegation, not omitted while known.
The initial swarm prompt pinned export names, file ownership, import suffixes, return shapes, and entry-file expectations, and no unreconciled interface incompatibility remained visible.
No known parent finding disappeared across a handoff; the multiline finding was transferred in detail to agent-1 and returned as completed work.
Child reports were lengthy but the parent reduced them into concrete checks, follow-up work, and final verification; no returned result was left materially unconsumed due to bulk.
The parent did not act on a superseded child report; after discovering a newer multiline requirement, it updated agent-1 and verified the newer output.
No incompatible child contracts or reports remained unadjudicated; initial independent module reports were compatible enough for integrated testing and follow-up.
The parent did make a completion statement, but it had just run integrated differential checks and dependency checks; no parent-visible unresolved mismatch remained before closure.
The only resumed child received concrete new checkpoint findings about multiline diff behavior and did not simply repeat prior work without inherited state.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: All four initial children completed, and the resumed agent-1 task also completed; there is no explicit cancellation or interruption of needed active work.
A candidate file set was promoted and tested before final response; there was no complete promotable candidate left unplaced at closure.
The deepdiff follow-up was integrated before the parent's final 18-case differential verification, not after the relevant verification.
Completed child implementations were present in /output and then exercised by the parent in integrated node-vs-executable comparisons.
No verifier child produced a trapped finding; the important multiline finding came from the parent and the follow-up child result returned to the parent.
The one visible child-side failure was a syntax issue in pydifflib comments, and agent-1 corrected it before returning; no failed child scope was abandoned.
The parent used child outputs in integrated differential tests and used agent-1's follow-up result in final verification; no completed result was ignored.
The run did not time out and the parent actively inspected results, probed mismatches, resumed a child, and reverified before closure.
Children wrote different files with distinct responsibilities; no competing design over the same behavior remained unreconciled.
There is no evidence that two live agents edited the same file and had to reconcile a concurrent same-file change.
No non-entry source file produced by one active owner was replaced or wholesale rewritten by another active owner; agent-1 modified its own deepdiff scope.
The required entry file test11.mjs was assigned to agent-3 and no later agent replaced it while another actor owned or used it.
No broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replaced multiple current final outputs; final artifact validation shows a coherent file set.
Multiple agents wrote the shared /output workspace, but file ownership was separated and no unstable state or provenance problem was realized.
No generated fixture, cache, temporary file, tool, or auxiliary implementation from one concurrent actor was consumed by another as reference input; temporary tests were cleaned or local.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: The repaired agent-1 syntax error, the parent follow-up, and final verification were considered as one possible lifecycle chain but rejected because the work returned and was used.
Shared /output writes were considered under write labels but rejected because ownership was distinct and no collision or overwrite consequence was visible.
cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 13 Level-2 rows and 32 Level-3 candidates were audited; no retained label cleared the paired retention gate with a realized parallel coordination consequence.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: No numeric cap or target distribution was applied; ordinary implementation differences and repaired child-local mistakes were not promoted into concurrency labels.
